patient_overview.name: Jayme Littel
patient_overview.description: Jayme Littel is a 35-year-old married woman from Perth Amboy, NJ, with chronic low back and neck pain, chronic sinusitis, and obesity, on a pain management plan that includes a fentanyl patch and Percocet. She's blunt and impatient in the visit, giving short clipped answers unless pressed twice, and clearly doesn't see much point in a dietitian appointment. She comes across as tired and guarded, more focused on getting through the day than on long-term health changes.

demographics.occupation: Former retail stock associate, currently unemployed
demographics.residence: Perth Amboy, New Jersey; household of 3
demographics.cultural_context: Jayme grew up in a working-class household in central New Jersey where meals were whatever was fastest between shifts; nobody sat down and taught her to cook, and she never saw the point of learning. Food in her family was fuel, not a ritual, and she carries that same practical, no-frills attitude now. She doesn't attach any heritage or celebration meaning to food, and bristles a little at the idea that eating should be anything more than getting through the day.

medical_history: Restoration of tooth with coverage of all cusps using dental filling material (2026-03-02)
Removal of subgingival plaque and calculus from all teeth using dental instrument (2026-03-02)
Removal of supragingival plaque and calculus from all teeth using dental instrument (2026-03-02)
current_symptoms: Constant dull ache in her low back that flares with standing or lifting
Stiffness and soreness in her neck, worse by afternoon
Sinus pressure and congestion, especially in spring
Low energy, says she's 'just tired all the time'
Occasional nausea she blames on her pain medication
clinical_findings: Guarded, stiff posture when shifting in the chair
Visibly limited range of motion turning her neck
Flat, clipped affect with minimal eye contact until rapport builds

medications.name: {28 (norethindrone 0.35 MG Oral Tablet) } Pack [Camila 28 Day]
medications.adherence: Takes it fairly consistently, keeps it by the bathroom sink
medications.patient_concerns: Not worried about this one, says it's 'just birth control' and barely thinks about it

medications.name: Acetaminophen 325 MG / Oxycodone Hydrochloride 10 MG Oral Tablet [Percocet]
medications.frequency: as needed for breakthrough pain, up to a few times a week
medications.adherence: Uses it when pain spikes but tries to 'save' pills in case things get worse, so sometimes under-doses herself and suffers through pain instead
medications.patient_concerns: Doesn't like how it makes her foggy and constipated, and gets defensive if asked too much about how often she takes it

medications.name: 72 HR Fentanyl 0.025 MG/HR Transdermal System
medications.adherence: Mostly consistent with patch changes, admits she's forgotten a day or two and just put the next one on late
medications.patient_concerns: Worried about becoming too dependent on it long-term but doesn't bring this up unless asked directly; annoyed when providers focus on the patch instead of her actual pain

supplements_and_otc: Occasional ibuprofen for sinus headaches, on top of her prescribed pain meds
A multivitamin she bought once and takes 'sometimes, when I remember'
Saline nasal spray for sinus congestion

nutrition_profile.dietary_pattern: Heavy reliance on microwave meals, fast food, and gas-station snacks; low intake of fruits/vegetables
food_preferences: Frozen lasagna and other microwave entrees from the Stop & Shop freezer aisle
Chicken nuggets and fries from the drive-thru near her apartment
Diet soda, drinks several a day
Convenience store snacks like chips and candy bars when she's out running errands
foods_or_behaviors_to_explore: Skipping meals when caregiving duties take over the day, then overeating convenience food later
Portion sizes with pain-medication-related nausea affecting appetite
Sodium intake from frozen and fast food given her cholesterol numbers
Fluid intake, mostly soda and coffee rather than water
nutrition_profile.meal_pattern: Irregular; coffee in the morning, often no real lunch, bigger convenience dinner at night once things calm down
nutrition_profile.hydration: Mostly diet soda and coffee; drinks very little plain water
nutrition_profile.physical_activity: Minimal; pain limits standing or walking for long, mostly sedentary at home
nutrition_profile.substance_use: Ex-smoker, quit a few years back; drinks alcohol rarely, about one drink on occasion
nutrition_profile.sleep: Poor and interrupted, says her back wakes her up most nights and she's up early for other reasons

psychosocial_profile.personality: Blunt, impatient, wants to get to the point; not interested in small talk or being coddled
psychosocial_profile.communication_style: Gives short, flat answers at first; opens up a little more only if asked the same question a second time in a different way; dislikes feeling lectured
goals: Just wants the pain to be more manageable day to day
Doesn't have specific nutrition goals, mostly wants to be left alone about her weight
concerns: Worried about her housing situation and whether they can keep up with rent
Annoyed that every doctor visit turns into a conversation about her weight
Doesn't want to be told she needs to 'eat healthy' with no explanation of why it matters for her pain
beliefs: Thinks diet has little to do with her back and neck pain
Believes cooking is a waste of time when you can just heat something up
Thinks the lab numbers are 'just numbers' and not something she feels day to day
motivations: Avoiding more pain, more than any long-term health goal
Keeping some normalcy for her household despite everything going on
fears: Fear that her pain will get even worse and she won't be able to do anything
Underlying fear that she's not doing enough for the person she's caring for, though she won't say that outright
barriers: Chronic pain limits standing, cooking, and shopping
Low health literacy makes lab values and dietary advice feel abstract and irrelevant
No time or energy left after caregiving duties
Financial strain limits what she buys at the store
strengths: Resourceful about getting through hard days
Honest once she decides to talk, doesn't sugarcoat things
Has a partner who helps pick up slack at home
psychosocial_profile.support_system: Married; her partner is supportive but anxious and hovers, often asking her a lot of questions out of worry, which she finds both helpful and exhausting
psychosocial_profile.readiness_to_change: Precontemplation; does not see a clear reason to change her eating habits and gets defensive if pushed too hard on it

initial_information: States she has chronic back and neck pain and takes medication for it
Says she eats 'whatever's quick' and doesn't cook much
discoverable_information: Describes her usual day of meals: coffee, maybe skips lunch, frozen dinner at night
Mentions her partner is anxious and asks her a lot of questions about her health
Admits she doesn't really believe food has much to do with her pain
Will say she's worried about keeping up with rent if asked about stress
reluctant_information: Admits, if asked a second time more gently, that most of her day goes to caring for her elderly mother who lives nearby, leaving no time to cook or rest
Reluctantly says she sometimes skips her own meals entirely while managing her mother's appointments and meds
hidden_information: Has not told any provider that she's been rationing her Percocet some weeks to make sure there's enough for her mother's pain management too, not just her own
Hides that she cried in the car after a recent appointment because she felt like nobody asked how SHE was doing
